newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 8.

text.p: Two major Mexican ports were shut as of 1000 local/1600 GMT Wednesday, including one of three key crude shipping ports, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in a daily update.

Pajaritos, under the jurisdiction of Coatzacoalcos in Veracruz state, was closed at 0650 local/1450 GMT because of dense fog. The port ships an average 400,000 barrels per day of crude for export, according to the latest oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) statistics.
Also in Veracruz, Frontera was shut amid winds between 40 and 50 km per hour.
Sailing was closed to smaller boats at Veracruz, Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche, Tampico, Tuxpan, El Mezquital and Altamira amid moderate wind speeds.
The report also warned against sailing in the Gulf of Mexico and the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of winds, rain and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

A cold front from southern Coahuila state bringing clouds and a slight chance of rain to the states of Sinaloa, Nayarit and Jalisco, where dominant winds from the northwest were 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/17 to 22 miles per hour) with waves five to eight feet high.

Light winds along the coasts of Michoacan and Guerrero, with winds from the southwest of 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves of five to seven feet high. In the Gulf of Tehuantepec northern winds were clocked at 20 to 30 knots (38 to 47 km/22 to 33 miles per hour) and waves were reported eight to 12 feet high.

A stationary cold front from the Florida peninsula moving south along the Gulf of Mexico and toward the center of the country, expected to reach the Yucatan peninsula later today. Winds from the north at 25 to 35 knots (47 to 66 km/28 to 39 miles per hour) and waves between nine and 13 feet high.
Humidity and light clouds along the coasts of Panama, Colombia and Venezuela with dominant winds from the east up to 10 to 15 knots with waves three to five feet high.
